title: I Run a Fleet of AI Agents Across Three Machines. Here's What Broke. - Kyle Jaejun Lee, KRAFTON
talk_summary: A solo operator scaled from a handful of tmux agents to a hierarchical fleet (CEO/VP/manager/worker) across three machines, and reports the concrete failures that forced each design change. The core transferable ideas are file-based state with reset-instead-of-compact, a blocking review gateway, and forcing delegation through a CLI harness.

takeaways.technique: Reset instead of compact, with handoff files
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of letting the model compact/summarize when the window fills, they clear context entirely and have the agent re-read mission/status/handoff files it wrote to disk, resuming from files rather than model memory.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I don't compact, I reset... it just reads back the handoff and the history files it wrote for itself and picks up exactly where it left off.

takeaways.technique: Hierarchy with scoped context and approval boundaries
takeaways.what_they_do: CEO/VP/manager/worker are real entity types, each with its own scoped context and approval boundary; context flows down, results flow up, and the human only reviews what reaches the top.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Each one is its own agent with its own scoped context and its own approval boundary. Context flows down.

takeaways.what_they_do: Orchestrators kept doing worker tasks themselves, so they wrapped dispatch in a CLI harness with skills that call those CLIs, making delegation the only available path.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A CLI harness with skills that call those CLIs. So dispatching becomes the only path it can take.

takeaways.technique: Single blocking review gateway with auto-resume
takeaways.what_they_do: Any layer submitting a plan blocks until approved in one web inbox; approval fires a hook that resumes the work automatically, so the human never walks into work windows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Any layer that wants to act submits its plan and then it blocks... the second I approve, a hook fires the work off automatically.

takeaways.what_they_do: Credentials collided and bound to wrong workspaces; fix was a fully separated environment per workspace. Also moved long-running work off the laptop to always-on Linux boxes and added a one-command boot that restores from files.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The fix was a clean, fully separated environment for each workspace.

takeaways.technique: Shared state via git PRs, per-machine dirs
takeaways.what_they_do: Context files are committed and pushed to move between machines; machine-specific state lives in per-machine directories and shared state only changes through a pull request to avoid silent divergence.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Per-machine directories for machine-specific state, and the shared stuff only changes through a pull request.
